contextweaver.title: Two debugging trajectories
contextweaver.intro: The paper compares these SWE-bench tasks over five paired runs each.

blocks.label: Django · Changes across files
blocks.text: The fix requires coordinated edits to several components. ContextWeaver retains the early architectural analysis; the sliding window often loses it and repeats exploration or makes incompatible partial fixes.

blocks.label: pytest · A change in one location
blocks.text: The fix is confined to one location in one file. Recent edit history is sufficient here. Extra branches in ContextWeaver’s memory divert attention from the immediate change.

contextweaver.provenance: Case descriptions and comparison outcomes paraphrased from Section 4.3.

qudsim.title: Different explanations, the same discourse role
qudsim.intro: Two models receive the same fictional story prompt. In both stories, a leader questions a secret and another character defends keeping it.

blocks.label: Question answered by both passages
blocks.text: What is the reason given for the deception?

blocks.label: Gemini Flash 1.5
blocks.text: Exposing the secret would threaten social stability.
blocks.note: The character defends concealment as protection against upheaval.

blocks.label: GPT-4o
blocks.text: A shared belief unites people and makes progress possible.
blocks.note: The character defends concealment as a way to maintain cooperation.

qudsim.provenance: Question from Figure 1. The two story passages are paraphrased.

qsalience.title: Questions after a cease-fire violation
qsalience.intro: A news report describes artillery fire in Grozny during a cease-fire. Annotators rated these two questions differently.

blocks.label: Q3 · Original question
blocks.text: What was the reason behind the artillery fire in Grozny on Tuesday despite the agreed cease-fire?
blocks.note: An explanation for the violation would help the reader assess the peace talks. A later sentence says the negotiators lack control over some fighters.

blocks.label: Q4 · Paraphrased question
blocks.text: What further details are available about the reported missile attacks?
blocks.note: More detail about the attack adds less to the reader’s understanding of the peace talks.

qsalience.provenance: Human ratings of GPT-4 questions. Q3 is quoted; Q4 and the rationales are paraphrased.

qudeval.title: When a question borrows from its answer
qudeval.intro: The questions below are meant to be answered by sentence 7, which introduces restrictions on nuclear exports. The preceding sentences describe accumulated nuclear material and export licenses.

blocks.label: ChatGPT · Anchor: sentence 5
blocks.text: What are the restrictions on nuclear exports and transfer of nuclear materials to a third country?
blocks.mark: transfer of nuclear materials to a third country
blocks.note: The marked detail appears only in the answer sentence. The anchor discusses accumulated nuclear material and does not raise this question.

blocks.label: Human DCQA annotation · Anchor: sentence 6
blocks.text: What restrictions exist on nuclear material exports?
blocks.note: The question follows the discussion of export licenses without introducing the later restriction.

qudeval.provenance: Questions, anchors, and error annotations from Figure 3; explanations paraphrased.

elabqud.title: The reason behind a skills gap
elabqud.intro: New jobs in New Haven require skills that many local young people lack. In the simplified article, the editor adds an explanation.

blocks.label: Implicit question
blocks.text: Why don’t people acquire the necessary skills?

blocks.label: Sentence added by the editor
blocks.text: Many do not have the money to get the training they need.

elabqud.provenance: Question and added sentence quoted from Figure 1. The article example is from Srikanth and Li (2021); context paraphrased.

qud-parsing.title: From an aid package to a funding gap
qud-parsing.intro: Sentence 4 answers a question raised by sentence 3. That question labels the dependency between them.

blocks.label: Sentence 3 · Anchor
blocks.text: The House approves a smaller relief package than California had requested.

blocks.label: Sentence 4 · Answer
blocks.text: California still faces a funding gap of roughly $2 billion to $4 billion.

qud-parsing.provenance: Annotated DCQA example in Figure 1(a). Question quoted; anchor and answer paraphrased.

bilingual-disfluencies.title: Which word comes before the pause?
bilingual-disfluencies.intro: These examples from the appendix show why the words before and after a pause are treated separately.

blocks.label: Pause after the noun
blocks.text: give me the stethoscope uhm to hear your heart
blocks.note: Preceding word: stethoscope. Following word: to.

blocks.label: Pause before the noun
blocks.text: give me the uhm stethoscope to hear your heart
blocks.note: Preceding word: the. Following word: stethoscope.

bilingual-disfluencies.conclusion: In the bilingual model, lower frequency of the preceding word is associated with between-word disfluencies. In the monolingual model, the corresponding association involves fewer phonological neighbors of the following word.
bilingual-disfluencies.provenance: Illustrative sentences from Appendix A.0.1, not participant transcripts. Feature interpretations paraphrased.
